generatedProse.concept-context: In any subject, reflective practice is what turns experience into development rather than just time served. Whatever the field, the people who keep improving are the ones who look back critically at what they did, weigh it against the standards they are working toward, and change something as a result. Treated this way, reflection is not a task to complete but the evaluation stage of regulating your own learning.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two students at the end of a demanding piece of work that did not go to plan.

Student A writes the episode up because it is required. The account is honest and complete: it says what happened, in order, and admits to feeling out of their depth. But Student A treats reflection as a box to tick. No reason is asked for, nothing is weighed against any standard, and nothing changes as a result. For Student A, reflection is compliance.

Student B writes the same episode up as someone examining their own practice. Student B asks why it went that way, weighs the choices made against what good work in the field demands, and traces the difficulty to thin preparation rather than bad luck. A specific conclusion follows, to prepare differently next time, and Student B commits to it. For Student B, the episode becomes development.

Both students reflected. Only Student B treated reflection as professional practice, using it to understand themselves and improve.
generatedProse.summary: In any subject, reflective practice is the engine of self-regulated development: the evaluation stage in which you look back critically at your own work against the standards of your field, and keep doing so across a career. You can now say why it matters, appraise how well someone reflects, and judge what owning it asks of you. The next lesson gives you a structure, Kolb's cycle, for reflecting critically on a single experience.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Student B's reflection professional practice rather than compliance?

items.text: Student B weighed their own choices against the standards of the field and committed to a specific change.
Student B produced a longer and more detailed account of what happened.
Student B completed the required write-up on time.
Student B described exactly what happened, in order.

feedback.correct: That's right. Weighing your practice against the standards of your field and committing to a change is reflection as development.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Student B did beyond recording the episode.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Student B's reflection was professional practice because it weighed the choices made against the field's standards and committed to a change, not because it was longer, on time or well ordered.

_prompts.concept-context: What does this look like in practice within the given context? Write a short follow-on from the generic definition above, in the learner's own subject or discipline. Keep it to two or three sentences, mid-register, following straight on from the generic definition.
_prompts.worked-example: Give a subject-specific worked example of this lesson's concept: a weaker or less-developed version first, then a stronger version reached by better practice, using the context cast (character tokens) consistently. Keep the weaker-then-stronger shape and the two-part contrast; name the cast directly in the prose (the pack supplies the whole body). The merge renders it as a block quote, so write it as continuous prose, not as a quoted comment plus commentary.
_prompts.summary: Recap what the learner can now do, in terms of their own subject or context. One short paragraph. Do not restate the learning outcomes verbatim.
_prompts.check: Write the subject's own version of this lesson's check question(s), testing the same outcome in the learner's own discipline. Keep the same number of items and the same correctness pattern as the generic version; reword the stem and items for the subject. Keep the component-level feedback (correct / notFinal / final) teaching, never a bare verdict.
